newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures settle higher before first notice day.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures settle higher before first notice day.

text.p: FCOJ futures closed firmer but off the highs ahead of the first notice day for the July contract on Tuesday.
Dealers said local and speculative buying of July contracts from 71.80 cents, carried the spot month to the day's high of 73.40 cents.
The contract ended 0.20 cent higher at 72.55 cents per lb, having ranged from 73.40 to 71.75 cents. September closed up 0.90 at 76.40 cents, while the outer months finished 0.85 lower to 1.00 firmer.
An estimated 5,000 lots changed hands on the day, compared with Friday's official 3,968 lots.
Total open interest remained high at 32,459 lots as of Friday, NYCE said. Players await Tuesday's spec/hedge report, which is expected to reflect an increasing speculative short position.

Meanwhile, the near-term outlook remains negative for prices, market analysts said. Support in the most-active September contract was pegged at 74.05 followed by 72.00 cents, where the contract should find a bottom and begin to rally.
"But until we close above the four, nine and 18-day moving averages," prices will remain weak technically, an analyst said.
The key numbers are 76.10 cents, 76.80 cents, and 78.35 cents, respectively.
